To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the current evaluation benchmarks for NLI are insufficient for evaluating the ability to understand discourse, 2) there is no clear correlation between performance on DiscEval and NLI, and 3) there are many ways to use DiscEval.

(i) DiscEval is a compilation of discourse-based datasets for evaluation of English NLU; (ii) DiscEval is useful for evaluation of English language understanding, and can be used as supplementary data for NLU training; (iii) The DiscEval dataset is publicly available.

the following tasks are important for evaluating language understanding: discourse, coreference, and temporal relations, and that NLI pretraining does not lead to learning really universal representations.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DiscEval datasets are a good starting point for discourse-based evaluation, but more data is still needed.
the DiscEval datasets can be used for a variety of purposes, and that the datasets can be used as an alternative to NLI for evaluating Natural Language Understanding.

the current state of the art in language understanding is still far from being able to understand language as humans do, and that there is a long way to go before we can claim that we are able to understand language at all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DiscEval is a collection of $11$ datasets that can be used to evaluate language understanding models, with an emphasis on discourse.
DiscEval is a compilation of $10$ datasets for discourse-based evaluation of Natural Language Understanding, and $1$ supplementary dataset for discourse-aware training.

the evaluation of language understanding is not complete without considering meaning as use, and that we need more discourse-based evaluation datasets to better understand the limits of current systems and to improve them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evaluation of language understanding should be done with tasks that require the use of language.
the evaluation of Natural Language Understanding should not focus solely on the NLI task, as this is not a sufficient proxy for discourse understanding.

the current state-of-the-art systems for NLI and discourse-based tasks have not converged yet, suggesting that there is room for improvement in the current approaches to NLI and discourse understanding.
